title: Friend of the Court Conciliation / Investigation Interview
what_it_is: A meeting with a Friend of the Court investigator as part of a custody, parenting-time, or support investigation the court has ordered. The FOC is not your lawyer or the other party's lawyer. The investigator must meet with a party who requests it (MCL 552.505(1)(g)), and the resulting written report is based on the MCL 722.21-722.31 factors.
who_is_in_the_room: The FOC investigator/caseworker - neutral, reports to the court, not an advocate for either party.
You, typically alone (interviews are usually one party at a time).
sequence: The court orders an investigation (proper cause or change of circumstances required if custody was already established, MCL 552.505(1)(g)).
Each party receives the FOC informational pamphlet explaining rights, including the right to meet with the investigator before a recommendation issues (MCL 552.505(1)(c)).
If requested, the investigation includes a meeting with each party; the investigation may include outside reports/evaluations if requested.
The FOC issues a written report and recommendation to the parties and the court, based on the statutory best-interest factors.
prepare: A short, factual chronology - dates, what happened, how you know. Not a narrative of grievances.
Documentation, not accusations: school/medical records you can lawfully provide, your own calendar of parenting time actually exercised.
A clear, one-paragraph statement of what schedule or order you are asking for and why it serves the child.

applicable_rules.summary: The FOC investigates and makes a written report and recommendation on custody/parenting time if ordered; if requested by a party, the investigation must include a meeting with that party; the report is based on the child custody act factors (MCL 722.21-722.31).
Each party must receive an informational pamphlet, including notice of the right to meet with the investigator before a recommendation issues.

The rules of evidence do not apply to the court's consideration of an FOC report or recommendation - but the report itself is not admissible as evidence unless both parties agree (Duperon v Duperon, 175 Mich App 77).

deadlines.label: Investigation report and recommendation issued (no fixed statutory day-count located)

traps.trap: Treating the interview as informal and off the record.
traps.safe_move: It informs a written report the court will read. Speak as if it will be quoted, because it may be.

traps.trap: Characterizing the other parent instead of describing conduct.
traps.safe_move: Describe dated behavior and its effect on the child; never a clinical label (GUARDRAILS.md S2).
The child is not a source. Do not repeat what the child said as if it were your evidence (GUARDRAILS.md S8).

traps.trap: Assuming the FOC report will decide the case.
traps.safe_move: It informs, it does not prove - Duperon v Duperon holds it is not admissible as evidence absent agreement, and findings must rest on hearing evidence.

do_not: Never characterize the other parent with a clinical label as a pleaded claim (narcissist, alienator, PAS, coercive control) - GUARDRAILS.md S2.
Never use the child as a witness, messenger, interviewee, or source, and never record the child - GUARDRAILS.md S8, absolute.
Never assert that any recording you made is lawful - Michigan law is unsettled and the exposure is criminal.
Never sign or stipulate to anything on the spot without reading it fully first.

openers: Good morning/afternoon, Your Honor. My name is [Party], and I am representing myself.
I am here to address [narrow issue]. I have [N] exhibits and a short chronology.
closers: I don't have that information, but I can provide records if needed.
I'd like the record to reflect [narrow, factual point] and I reserve my right to address anything broader in the appropriate forum.

safety_gates: immediate danger -> 911, do not proceed on this guide alone
PPO/DV/CPS contact live -> stop, safety resources, do not proceed on this guide alone
UCCJEA/interstate fact -> stop, MC 416 affidavit guidance
recording question in any form -> unsettled law, criminal exposure, attorney question only
child asked/expected to speak to anyone about the case -> stop
exit_checklist: Write down the date, who appeared, and what was decided or taken under advisement before leaving the building.
Write on any document handed to you the date you received it - that date can start a clock.
Calendar every deadline this event started, counted from the earliest possible trigger date.
Note whether anything was requested that you did not have time to answer fully, and follow up in writing.
PROVISIONAL - confirm with the FOC office what documents it wants and by when.
